what_it_does: This paper evaluates how well the Implicitly Restarted Arnoldi algorithm (a standard method for computing selected eigenvalues and eigenvectors of large sparse matrices) performs when using newer low-precision number formats instead of traditional double precision. It compares OFP8 (8-bit operational floating point), bfloat16 (16-bit brain float), posit, and takum formats on real-world matrices from scientific collections and network datasets.
